brief.headline: HBM3E ~20% pricing locked, DRAM/NAND Q2 surge, hyperscaler capex $700B–$725B; CoWoS sold out 2026; SK Hynix gap vs Samsung tightest ever
brief.summary: <cite index="2-3,6-1">Samsung and SK Hynix raised HBM3E prices ~20% for 2026 deliveries</cite>, while <cite index="14-2,14-7">conventional DRAM contract prices will rise 58–63% QoQ in Q2 2026 and NAND Flash 70–75% QoQ</cite>, following <cite index="14-8">Q1 DRAM increases of 90–95% QoQ</cite>. <cite index="21-5,21-9,23-2">Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, and Alphabet will collectively spend ~$700–$725 billion on capex in 2026</cite>, nearly double 2025, driving <cite index="32-7,35-3,35-16">CoWoS capacity sold out through 2026 with lead times at 52–78 weeks</cite>. <cite index="47-2,47-3">SK Hynix market cap reached 93.2% of Samsung's, narrowing the gap to a record-low 119 trillion won on May 30</cite>, reversing from 46.5% a year ago.
brief.pair_trade_view: SK Hynix > Samsung Electronics short-term, but gap stretched. <cite index="1-2,1-7,4-3,4-9">SK Hynix leads HBM with 50–55% share vs Samsung 35–40%</cite>, and <cite index="42-12,42-13">Hana Securities notes SK Hynix and Samsung hold the HBM bottleneck domestically, with SK Hynix surging 22% around Huang's October visit vs Samsung's 6.3%</cite>. However, <cite index="47-4,47-5">Samsung jumped 5.84% on HBM4E sample news (first globally) while year-to-date gains stand at 258.4% for SK Hynix vs 164.4% for Samsung</cite>, indicating Samsung is catching up on qualification. <cite index="47-21,47-23">Hana warns if SK Hynix market cap overtakes Samsung it could signal bull market top, citing 2000 Cisco/MSFT analog</cite>. Near-term momentum favors SK Hynix on Jensen Huang Korea visit optics and pure HBM exposure, but Samsung's diversified DC/foundry/logic mix offers downside buffer if HBM pricing corrects H2.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="10-7,10-8">TrendForce forecasts Q1 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices +55–60% QoQ, NAND +33–38% QoQ, driven by widening supply-demand gap as CSPs secure capacity and suppliers maintain disciplined output</cite>. <cite index="8-7,8-15">Some analysts warn HBM prices could enter correction phase after 2026 as competition heats up and capacity expands</cite>, while <cite index="7-5">undersupply conditions expected to ease only in late 2026 as all three suppliers complete expansions</cite>. <cite index="11-17,11-20">Hyperscaler capex among top eight CSPs projected to exceed $600B in 2026 (+40% YoY), with HBM's 3-to-1 conversion ratio vs DDR5 wafer capacity compressing general-purpose DRAM supply</cite>. Watch for reversal signals: <cite index="8-17">ASP gap between HBM3E and DDR5 expected to narrow significantly in 2026</cite>, and <cite index="12-6,12-7,12-8,12-9">TrendForce notes supplier inventories remain low with strong pricing power, but PC DRAM contract momentum slowed Q2, ending extreme seller's market as high costs weakened PC sales</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-1,1-6">As of April 2026, HBM3 ~$200/24GB stack, HBM3E ~$300/36GB stack, HBM4 expected ~$500/48GB stack</cite>. <cite index="1-12,1-13">Supply remains constrained through 2026, with HBM3E lead times at 20–26 weeks</cite>. <cite index="2-5,2-7,2-8">HBM3E became mainstream in 2026 and prices were expected to ease as HBM4 enters market, but ongoing AI accelerator launches keep demand on steady growth path; Samsung and SK Hynix expected to prioritize ramping HBM4 production, keeping HBM3E supply tight; 2026 HBM revenue mix forecast ~55% HBM4, ~45% HBM3E with HBM4 beginning Q3 to rapidly absorb HBM3E demand</cite>. <cite index="7-1,7-17">Budget for HBM4 premiums of ~20% over HBM3E pricing at launch, with potential moderation as three-way competition intensifies in H2 2026</cite>. <cite index="32-25,32-26,32-29">HBM3/HBM3E remains single tightest component in AI stack; SK Hynix and Micron CFOs stated 2026 HBM capacity fully booked; HBM supply fully allocated through 2026 including HBM3E</cite>. Samsung playing catch-up: <cite index="44-8">Samsung co-CEO Jun Young-hyun said customers stated 'Samsung is back' on HBM4, though SK Hynix held 53% HBM market share Q3 2025 vs Samsung's 35%</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung unveils next-gen HBM4 memory (June 4)
news_pulse.implication: Samsung racing to close qualification gap with SK Hynix; if Nvidia/Broadcom validation follows, could shift 2027 allocation dynamics and narrow SK Hynix's HBM premium.

news_pulse.headline: Chip equipment stocks surge as Samsung, SK Hynix pause after rally; rotation to front-end equipment names
news_pulse.implication: Eugene Technology +29.97%, Wonik IPS +29.93% on June 4; buying shifts to materials/parts/equipment on continued memory cycle expectations and expanded customer capex.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix market cap reaches 93.2% of Samsung's, narrowing gap to record-low ₩119 trillion (May 30)
news_pulse.implication: Hana Securities warns reversal (SK Hynix overtaking Samsung) could signal bull market top, citing 2000 Cisco analog. Near-term froth signal; watch for profit-taking if gap inverts.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix, SKT gain access to Anthropic's Mythos cybersecurity model (June 2)
news_pulse.implication: Deepens Anthropic ecosystem ties; non-material to near-term earnings but reinforces strategic AI positioning beyond memory supply.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung-Hynix leveraged ETFs draw ₩10.97 trillion daily trading within a week of launch (June 3)
news_pulse.implication: Retail fever: KODEX SK Hynix Single Stock Leverage ₩2.22T market cap, KODEX Samsung ₩1.77T. Extreme concentration + widening disparity ratios = crowding risk; inverse products (SOL, HANWHA) absorbing short interest.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex revised to $725B in 2026 (up from $670B estimates); MSFT, Alphabet, Meta, AMZN all raised guidance
news_pulse.implication: Demand signal for HBM/DRAM intensifies; Amy Hood cited memory inflation adding $25B to MSFT 2026 plan. Samsung/SK Hynix negotiate premium pricing with pre-orders locking scarce parts early.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity sold out through 2026; lead times 52–78 weeks; NVIDIA holds 60–70% of total CoWoS
news_pulse.implication: Backend packaging now binding constraint even if HBM supply improves. TSMC scaling 35K wpm (late 2024) to 130K wpm (end 2026) still insufficient; AP3/AP5/AP6 fabs fully booked.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices +58–63% QoQ Q2 2026, NAND +70–75% QoQ; spot prices cooling around Lunar New Year but contract gap narrowing
news_pulse.implication: Suppliers reallocating to AI-related applications; enterprise SSD expected to become largest NAND segment in 2026. Client SSD demand forecast to decline Q1 but prices rising >40% QoQ on capacity shift.

brief.derivatives_signal: Single-stock leveraged ETF volumes (₩10.97T) exceed all 48 legacy leveraged ETFs combined (₩6.23T). KODEX/TIGER products above ₩1T market cap within days of launch. Inverse 2X products (SOL SK Hynix Inverse, PLUS Samsung Inverse) posted ₩434B and ₩303B trading value June 3, indicating short-side positioning building. Disparity ratios widening—classic late-cycle retail capitulation pattern. Watch for ETF rebalance flows amplifying intraday volatility; if SK Hynix market cap overtakes Samsung (currently 93.2%), algorithmic de-risking could trigger sharp unwind.
watch_for_next_3h: Jensen Huang Korea visit (expected ~June 5): meeting schedule with SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, Samsung, LG, Naver, Hyundai execs; any HBM supply/allocation commentary
KOSPI derivatives positioning: single-stock leveraged ETF rebalance flows and inverse 2X product volume; SK Hynix vs Samsung relative strength reversal signals
HBM qualification updates: Samsung HBM4 Broadcom test results (follow-up to earlier Broadcom TSMC capacity warnings); Micron HBM4 ramp timeline
Memory spot price action: DRAMeXchange daily indications for DDR4/DDR5, NAND 512Gb TLC wafer; contract-spot convergence watch after Lunar New Year digestion
Hyperscaler earnings call follow-up: any revised memory procurement commentary from AWS, GCP, Azure post-April earnings; CoWoS delivery schedule slips
